The inspiration for finally making his music came when he was in a near-fatal car crash.

With grand production that sounds like the natural evolution of all the albums that came before it, this is seen by many as Ye's best album, even earning an extremely rare 10/10 rating from Pitchfork. The recording process was finished by October 2010, according to Ye in a tweet. Most tracks were made in Avex in Honolulu, Hawaii, where Ye flew out artists and producers to work on the album. Said sessions also had "Commandments", that prohibited Tweeting, taking pictures, and wearing hipster hats.

He swapped lush soul and anthemic hooks for splintering electro, acid house, and industrial force while packaging some of his most lewd and heart-crushing tales. Initially envisioned as Thank God For Drugs, a much larger project, Ye would play the album for Rick Rubin, he later recalled listening to roughly 3-hours of unfinished material that seemed to need months worth of work - despite the release date being a month away. Ye enlisted Rubin to refine and complete the project, finishing a majority of the songs just two days before release.
